To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

follistatin and follitatin-related gene are expressed in normal breast tissue and in breast proliferative disorders; follistatin expression in the stromal component is increased in fibroadenoma; follitatin-related protein expression is increased in the epithelial component in ductal carcinoma.

follistatin and its binding protein FLRG are differentially expressed in normal breast and in different proliferative breast diseases, suggesting a role for these proteins in the development and progression of breast cancer.

follistatin and follstatin-related gene (FLRG), which bind and neutralize the antiproliferation activity of activins, are differentially expressed in normal and proliferative breast tissue, with follistatin up-regulation in fibroadenoma and FLRG over-expression in infiltrating ductal breast cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of follistatins in breast tissue and its role in breast cancer progression.
the expression of activin binding proteins, follistatin and follitatin related gene, in breast proliferative disorders, and their possible role in the progression of human breast malignancy.
the expression of follistain and FLRG in breast proliferative disorders and its possible role in the progression of the disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FST and FLGR expression is up-regulated in human breast proliferating diseases and their expression is associated with a more malignant phenotype of breast cancer.
follistatin and follitatin-related protein expression is increased in breast proliferative disease, and that this increase may counteract the antiproliferation effects of activin.
FST and FLGR are expressed in all breast diseases investigated, but their expression pattern is different and suggests a role for these proteins in the progression of human breast malignancy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FST and FLGR may be considered as markers of breast proliferative disease, and their expression may be related to the progression of breast tumors.
follistatin and follitropin receptor gene are up-regulated in human breast cancer.
follistatin and FST-like protein (FLRG) expression are up-regulated in human breast cancer and that this up-regulation is associated with a poor prognosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Follistatin is a potential target in breast cancer treatment.
follistatin and its related protein FLRG might be involved in breast tumor development and progression.
follistatin expression is increased in breast fibroadenoma, suggesting a possible role in the development of these benign tumors.
